Using This Bookp5

Here's what you'll find in this book:

  • Chapter 1: Playing the Game. The first chapter explains the fundamentals of the game, with examples to help you understand how to play.

  • Chapter 2: Creating a Character. Chapter 2 walks you through the steps of character creation.

  • Chapter 3: Character Classes. Characters' capabilities are largely determined by class, such as Fighter or Wizard. Chapter 3 offers twelve classes to choose from, along with forty-eight subclasses.

  • Chapter 4: Character Origins. Background and species are key elements in defining a character's origin, which further shapes the character's abilities beyond the choice of class. Background and species options are presented in chapter 4.

  • Chapter 5: Feats. The feats in chapter 5 are special features that characters gain as part of their background and class.

  • Chapter 6: Equipment. Armor, weapons, and adventuring gear are found in chapter 6.

  • Chapter 7: Spells. This chapter contains descriptions of the spells that spellcasters can cast.

  • Appendix A: The Multiverse. Here you'll find an overview of the magical multiverse where D&D adventures take place.

  • Appendix B: Creature Stat Blocks. This appendix brims with game information for creatures that certain characters can befriend or transform into.

  • Appendix C: Rules Glossary. The game's main rules terminology is summarized in this appendix, making it an invaluable reference during play.

Worlds of Adventurep5

The worlds of D&D glimmer with magic, monsters, and spectacular adventure. Launching from a foundation of medieval fantasy, these worlds soar with possibilities beyond those of our reality.

D&D worlds exist in a multiverse and are connected to one another and to other planes of existence. Some of the worlds have been published as official D&D settings, including the Greyhawk, Forgotten Realms, Dragonlance, Spelljammer, Planescape, Dark Sun, Eberron, and Ravenloft settings. Alongside these worlds are thousands more, created by generations of D&D players for their own games. Amid the richness of the multiverse, you might create a world of your own.

The worlds of the multiverse share characteristics, but each world is set apart by its own history and geography. Your DM might set a campaign on one of these worlds or on a world of their own invention. Because there is so much variety among D&D worlds, check with your DM about the world of your upcoming adventures.

What's new in the 2024 Version?p5

This is the 2024 version of the fifth edition Player's Handbook. If you've read the 2014 version, much of this book will feel familiar, since the fundamental rules of the game are the same. But the book contains many new or redesigned elements, and the versions of things in this book replace versions from older books. Here are highlights:

  • Streamlined Rules: The game's rules have been streamlined and are now supported by a rules glossary.

  • Easier Character Creation: Using chapter 2, making a character is easier than ever before.

  • Enhanced Classes: In chapter 3, every class and subclass has been enhanced with new options.

  • Reimagined Origins: Explored in chapter 4, a character's origin is now defined by background and species, each of which has been redesigned.

  • Expanded Feats: In chapter 5, feats have been redesigned, with many feats added.

  • Upgraded Weapons, Tools, and Crafting: Mastery properties transform how weapon wielders use their weapons, and every character can enjoy new tool and crafting rules in chapter 6.

  • Dazzling Spells: Chapter 7 bursts with new spells and old ones that have been enhanced.

If you can't find a rule, check the index. If a rule's name has changed from what was printed in the 2014 Player's Handbook, the index points you to the new name. For example, if you look up Inspiration in the index, it points you to the rules for Heroic Inspiration in the rules glossary.

Session 29 - “Egg-scape from Demogorgon” 3/27/26

Played this session: Daterra, Perry, Sig, Jibjib, Kronk

Before session 30, level up to Level 8!


Next Time. 

Current Objectives: 

  • Find your Stolen Things.

  • Find out who framed you for stealing things from Hourglass Coven hag sisters.

  • Find the missing unicorn horn to unfreeze Zybilna in her palace.

  • End the Hags’ tyranny over Prismeer.

  • Solve Bavlorna's Big Book of Bad Blood.

  • Solve the Puzzle Box.

  • Rescue remaining kids from Loomlurch: Mishka, Sigh, Puddlemore, Squid, Elkhorn.

  • Stop the demons pouring into the Underdark from the Abyss.

  • Solve the Ollie copies plot. “Radnelac”, “Smite”, etc.

  • Bring Nib furnishings for his home.

  • Go to Gracklstugh (the capital city of the gray dwarves), Skab wants a captive dragon investigated and preferably freed from the dwarves. 

  • Go to Neverlight Grove (home of the myconids like Shrump), Skab wants Daterra to collect spores or mushrooms from the heart of the grove and bring back to her for her alchemical experiments. 

  • Go to Blingdenstone (Sig's hometown and capital city of the deep gnomes), Skab wants a so-called "king" there investigated in case he is a threat to Skab and others.


Mysteries & Leads: 

  • Rifts between Underdark, Feywild, and Abyss. “Faerzress” and “fairy circles” amplified.

  • Jibjib learned of conspiracies from his Patron. Also warned to return to Underdark asap.

  • Demons are pouring into the Underdark through portals for some reason.

  • Zybilna and/or her Palace staff members have powerful magic items, make magic circles, and know about defeating/trapping demons.


Session 28 - “It Was a Trap!” 2/6/26

Played this session: Daterra, Perry, Sig, Jibjib, Kronk

  • Sig recognized where they were: the Whorlstone Tunnels beneath the dwarven city Gracklstugh. Sig realized after Riftwalking here, it seemed to be a big coincidence that they happened to fall directly into a deadly pit of zombies.

  • Runk the Derro. After escaping the zombie pit, the Party had the little derro guy, named Runk, restrained. Runk was terrified and confused about Daterra's Demogorgon forehead scar, but he agreed to take them to his master, a derro named Narrak. But Runk refused to lead the way, scared of all the dangers in the tunnels.

  • Yellow Mold. The Party encountered Yellow Mold hazards that damaged Daterra. They were able to jump or toss everyone past.

  • Traps. Daterra fell into a pit trap in the ground. Then they found a Shrieker, a mushroom that screams in alarm when approached. Daterra was able to speak to the mushroom to silence it before it screamed.

  • Approaching the Cult Ritual. With Sig and Jib disguised as derros, and Kronk and Perry acting as Daterra's bodyguards, the Party convinced the derros that Daterra was a cult leader needing to talk to Narrak. This allowed them to get in close to a group of derros performing a demonic ritual in a huge magic circle. Perry then walked right up… and slapped Narrak in the face for not honoring “cult leader” Daterra!

  • Combat. Narrak and his derro cultists attacked using demonic tentacles and psychic attacks. A two-headed giant, or “ettin”, also attacked, but the Party avoided having a Death Dog loosed from its cage. Jibjib kept a safe distance, using blasts, summons, and Hunger of Hadar within the entire magic circle. Sig gave massive healing. Perry tanked up close. Daterra summoned an elemental but was then KO'd. Kronk also got targeted a ton, getting frozen by Hold Person. But then in the end Kronk was unleashed and slaughtered enemies, including killing Narrak and Spartan-kicking him backward into Jibjib's Hadar tentacle darkness. Epic.

  • The Ritual Magic Circle. The magic circle used by Narrak and the derros had a couple statues in the center. The cultists were doing some ritual to curse certain stone giants in the city above by making them grow second heads and go Mad.

  • Sig Madness. After combat, Sig did some mysterious rituals for Mr. Sixx. Walking within the cultist magic circle gave Sig a Madness that made him forget the existence of everyone around. Exhausted and confused, Sig simply set up camp in the corner of the cavern. Unsure what else to do, the rest of the Party rested there too.

  • Shuushar's Betrayal. During the night, Shuushar visited Kronk for one last "Jedi training" dream, telling him the tale of “the Tragedy of Belaphoss the Mad”, a lieutenant of Demogorgon. It was revealed that Shuushar had been fattening the Party up to sacrifice them to his master, Demogorgon! HE helped Jorlan the drow guard summon demons at Velkenvelve in the very beginning, helping the Party break out of prison... HE was the one that sacrificed his entire city of Sloobludop to Demogorgon when he summoned his master there... He was "leveled up" with better stats and granted the ability to speak Common by his master... He had been faking being a pacifish, being wise and enlightened and prophetic... HE was the one helping to divert Sig to Riftwalk right into a pit of zombies in the Whorlstone Tunnels when trying to Rift to Gracklstugh... It's always... been... a trap!

  • Demogorgon Summoned. Sig, still under the effects of Madness that made him forget the existence of everyone else, was bound in Shuushar's net in his sleep. Meanwhile Shuushar transformed -- his head splitting apart in two and tentacles sprouting all over! Shuushar managed to summon his master Demogorgon using the cultist ritual circle while the Party rested in the cavern.

  • Next Time. Demogorgon is currently breaking through the wall of the cavern, trying to get at the Party! Shuushar is attacking Sig and Kronk! The Party must now try to escape...
